naya.title: Superbrain 10/10 Execution Cycle — Naya Note
naya.summary: The Superbrain moved from protocol toward executable enforcement through an authoritative CI gate, duplicate audit, rebuildable relationship graph, deterministic regression tests, retrieval smoke testing, Daily CIS smoke testing, and a machine-enforced execution-continuity contract.
lessons: The Superbrain must enforce its laws in code and CI, not merely document them.
Derived relationship graphs must be rebuildable from canonical events.
Green must be observed, not inferred.
A deliberate failing test is valuable evidence because it proves the guard can expose a missing contract.
next_best_actions: Resolve any failing gate step at root cause.
Then implement safe automated duplicate/entity resolution, contradiction handling, and semantic retrieval benchmarks.

human.title: Superbrain 10/10 Execution Cycle — Shawn Note
human.summary: We are turning the Superbrain from instructions into an executable system that checks itself. The brain-gate now validates memory, duplicate safety, relationships, continuity, retrieval, and Daily CIS before the system can claim success.
lessons: The brain has to prove that it works.
Readable human output and deterministic machine enforcement both matter.
A failure that identifies a real missing contract is progress, not something to hide.
next_best_actions: Get the gate genuinely green, then push the next three highest-value intelligence capabilities.

evidence: Regression suite created and wired into CI.
Relationship graph rebuild created and wired into CI.
Execution continuity enforcement created and wired into CI.
First enforcement run deliberately exposed missing verification and handoff on this event; event was repaired to represent an explicit in-progress state.
